_readme: Mutations for scripts/watch-red.py -- see rule 7 of CONTRIBUTING.md. Each entry breaks exactly one thing a guard claims to catch. `old` must appear exactly once in `file`; the test picked by `select` must go red, and its output must name `expect`, or the guard is red for the wrong reason and does not count as watched.

mutations.note: The trap the rule exists for. `schema/` reads as the workspace directory init creates and matches the packaged one four levels down; nothing about it shows in `git status`.

mutations.note: Without the flag git declines to consider a tracked path, so a check whose input is exactly the tracked paths reports nothing however wrong the rules are. This is the mutation that makes the other .gitignore guard mean something.

mutations.note: `.gitignore` is the one init output this repository cannot hold back -- the rule would have to ignore a tracked file to reach it. The exemption in test_gitignore.py is only safe while this stays true.

mutations.label: an asset URL that follows /releases/latest/ instead of the tag
mutations.new:
chmod +x nextbrief.pyz
# or, for whatever is newest:
# curl -fsSLO https://github.com/hancheng-ai/nextbrief/releases/latest/download/nextbrief.pyz
mutations.note: Anchored on a version-free line so the manifest survives a bump. `/releases/latest/` stopped being a 404 at 0.2.0 and started being something worse: it resolves to the newest non-prerelease while every other version string on the page is swept to the last tag, so tagging a candidate makes the page name one version and serve another.

mutations.label: the mark served from a third-party CDN
mutations.note: The rule this guard used to enforce was 'no http on the mark's line', which forced a broken image on PyPI and could not be satisfied any other way. What is actually worth refusing is a host that is not this repository -- somebody else's uptime, somebody else's log -- and jsdelivr is the plausible way that happens.

mutations.label: the mark back on a bare relative path
mutations.note: The defect that prompted the change. README.md is PyPI's long description, so a relative src has nowhere to resolve and renders as a broken image above the fold on the page most new users land on -- and it looks perfectly fine on GitHub, which is where it gets reviewed.

mutations.label: the mark pinned to main instead of the tag
mutations.note: PyPI keeps every version's long description forever, so a main-pinned URL breaks every historical release page the day that file moves. Green on GitHub, and invisible until somebody opens an old release.

mutations.label: the release badge left behind by a hand-edited version
mutations.expect: the release badge does not say
mutations.note: The badge is a static claim about which release this page documents, kept honest by the sweep. This is what it looks like when the sweep stops reaching it: every URL on the page moves and the badge does not.

mutations.label: the pinned brew install documented against a stale digest
mutations.note: What shipped for four releases: the formula's version was swept, its sha256 was not, and the README went on printing the command that downloads one and checks it against the other.

mutations.label: a relative link back on the page PyPI renders
mutations.expect: README.md links 'LICENSE' as a relative path
mutations.note: The reported defect, in its smallest form. README.md is PyPI's long description and PyPI renders it with no base URL, so a relative target resolves against the project page: the 'example workspace' link arrived as https://pypi.org/project/nextbrief/examples/workspace and 404'd. Anchored version-free, and deliberately left looking correct on GitHub -- which is where the page gets reviewed, and why 33 of these survived a release.

mutations.label: a relative link back on the Chinese page only
mutations.expect: README.zh.md links 'LICENSE' as a relative path
mutations.note: One of a translated pair edited and the other not is how these two files actually drift, so the rule has to be enforced on both rather than on the one PyPI happens to render today.

mutations.label: a link copied out of the address bar, pinned to main
mutations.expect: is a branch rather than a release tag
mutations.note: The plausible way the fix decays: absolute is the rule people remember, and the URL in the browser's address bar is /blob/main/. It resolves today, which is exactly the problem -- PyPI keeps every version's description forever, so it breaks the page of every past release the day that file moves.

mutations.label: a tag-pinned link to a path that is no longer there
mutations.expect: INVENTORY_SCHEMA_v2.md is not a file in this checkout
mutations.note: Absolute, tag-pinned, and 404. The sweep moves these links onto each new tag, so a file renamed without the README following it is not a stale link -- it is a broken one, on the next release.

mutations.label: the release-table citation pattern back on its pre-absolute anchor
mutations.note: This one already happened. Absolutising the links put a https://github.com/.../blob/vX.Y.Z/ in front of every CHANGELOG target, `](CHANGELOG` stopped matching, and the test kept passing on an empty loop -- rule 7's first shape, caused by a change three files away that had no reason to look at it. The sentinel, not the pattern, is what this mutation is watching.

mutations.label: the formula stops recording which release its digest is from
mutations.note: The digest is the one version literal here that no script can sweep, so the provenance line is the only thing that can tell a stale one from a current one. Losing it puts the repository back where it was: sixty-four hex characters and no way to date them.

mutations.label: the engine check is no longer the first thing run
mutations.note: Position is what the guard measures. Install guidance below three commands that have already failed is guidance nobody reaches.

mutations.label: the skill stops saying how to install the engine

mutations.label: the skill names the wrong exit code for a missing engine
mutations.note: First written against the phrase "command not found", which the skill happens to use twice; the mutation that deleted the sentence that mattered left the incidental mention behind and the guard stayed green. The number appears once and is checked against the code the shell really returns.

mutations.label: the skill offers to install the engine itself
mutations.old: **Tell the person; do not run the install yourself.**
mutations.new: **Tell the person, or install it for them if they are in a hurry.**

mutations.note: Both URLs are real and both return 200, so a fetch proves nothing here. Only the pairing does.
